# Branch cleanup queue.
# Replace the entries below in a pull request; do not append a new batch to stale entries.
# The Branch Cleanup workflow deletes exactly the non-comment lines after merge.
# Clear a completed queue through a follow-up pull request because main is PR-protected.
# See BRANCH_AUDIT.md for the canonical safe-delete list.

# --- Batch: provably-redundant refs (2026-08-07) ---
# The previous batch (16 archive/* duplicates) was merged as #425 and the
# workflow deleted all 16; verified against the live remote afterwards. Those
# lines are replaced here rather than appended, per the rule above.
#
# Every ref below is redundant under one of three mechanical proofs, re-run
# against main 696b2b547 immediately before this commit. No ref below has an
# open pull request — checked against the live open-PR head list.
#
#   (A) SQUASH-MERGED — the branch tip's tree hash appears verbatim in main's
#       own history, so main once contained exactly this content:
#           git log --format=%T origin/main | grep -x $(git rev-parse origin/<b>^{tree})
#       git's own --merged finds only one of these, because a squash merge
#       rewrites the commit and breaks ancestry while preserving the tree.
#
#   (B) EXACT DUPLICATE — two refs point at the identical tip commit. The
#       surviving name is recorded per line.
#
#   (C) STRICT ANCESTOR — every commit on the branch is already contained in a
#       live branch that carries more:
#           git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<b> origin/<survivor>
#
# Deleting these loses no reachable commit: in every case the content is still
# carried by main or by a named live branch.
#
# NOT queued, though the earlier audit proposed them: codex/x and
# feat/map-v1-v2-v3-upgrades are exact duplicates of each other, but nothing in
# the repo indicates which name is intended to survive — that needs a human.
# codex/best-ai-hardware, agent/codex/tallinn-tribe-studio-20260714 and
# agent/claude/v0-blueprint are all strictly contained in other branches but
# each has an OPEN PR (#284, #278, #336), so they stay.
